**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the gain-of-function mutations in SCN9A and SCN2A do not converge on the shared pathway of neuronal excitability regulation, or that the specific variants identified in patients do not lead to increased channel activity. _(variant: High allele frequency (>1%) of the specific gain-of-function variants in SCN9A or SCN2A in the gnomAD database.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of disrupted neuronal excitability via sodium channel dysfunction could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting these channels or downstream signaling pathways to treat both primary erythermalgia and episodic ataxia.
